IntelliDocs: An Intelligent Document Editing System for Academic Manuscripts

A Capstone Project Presented to the Faculty of the College of Computer Studies

CHAPTER 1

INTRODUCTION

Background of the Study

Students spend many hours formatting theses by hand, and small inconsistencies in headings and spacing are among the most common reasons a manuscript is returned for revision.

The main objective of this study is to reduce the time students spend formatting academic documents by learning each writer's formatting habits and applying them automatically.

Statement of the Problem

This study aims to answer the following questions:

1. How long do students spend formatting a thesis manually?

2. Which formatting errors are most common in submitted manuscripts?

3. How accurate are the system's formatting suggestions?

Significance of the Study

The results benefit students, advisers and panel members by shortening the review cycle for formatting issues.

Scope and Delimitation

The study covers documents written in English by undergraduate students and excludes handwritten submissions.

CHAPTER 2

REVIEW OF RELATED LITERATURE

Earlier work on document assistants focused on grammar correction rather than layout and structure.

Conceptual Framework

The framework links behavioral tracking, prediction and user feedback in a continuous loop.
